endorsements.title: CHAI Responsible AI Guide (Assurance Standards Guide)
endorsements.quote: Decisions made to change use context or the targeted population outside the intended or initially evaluated use can alter the effectiveness of the algorithm and require reevaluation.

endorsements.title: Machine Learning for Predicting Biologic Agent Efficacy in Ulcerative Colitis: An Analysis for Generalizability and Combination with Computational Models
endorsements.quote: Therefore, a model for patients receiving different doses or regimens of ustekinumab should be evaluated, and the impact of drug exposure or pharmacokinetic parameters on the model performance should be explored.

endorsements.title: From Data Stewardship to Model Stewardship: Extending Governance Frameworks for AI Era Health Data Use
endorsements.quote: (2) cross-institutional validation before deployment beyond the training context;

evidence.title: External Validation of a Machine Learning Model to Predict Postpartum Hemorrhage in a US Northeastern Healthcare System
evidence.outcome: re-evaluation in new health system
evidence.effect: External validation showed substantially reduced performance; AUC 0.60 (95% CI, 0.58– 0.61).
evidence.quote: The original CSL model demonstrated modest discrimination for predicting PPH with an AUC of 0.60 (95% CI, 0.58– 0.61).

evidence.title: Recalibration of a Non-Laboratory-Based Risk Model to Estimate Pre-Diabetes/Diabetes Mellitus Risk in Primary Care in Hong Kong
evidence.venue: Journal of primary care & community health
evidence.outcome: Model calibration when extended to a new population (primary care) with different pre-test probability
evidence.effect: Original model underestimated risk in the primary care population (intercept 1.79, slope 0.74). Simple recalibration adapted it to the new population. All updated models had AUC-ROC 0.742-0.750 versus 0.746 for the original.
evidence.quote: The simple recalibration method can adapt the HK Chinese pre-DM/DM model to PC populations with different pre-test probabilities.

evidence.title: Validation of a prediction model for postpartum hospital use in geographic contexts with greater rural representation
evidence.venue: American journal of obstetrics & gynecology MFM
evidence.outcome: Model performance when extended to new geographic populations, before and after updating
evidence.effect: NYC model overestimated risk in SC/FL but modest updating yielded well-calibrated models with AUC 0.69-0.70.
evidence.quote: Modest model updating, including recalibration of intercepts and re-estimation of coefficients, yielded well-calibrated models without requiring new predictors.

evidence.title: Assessment of the CLOT (children's likelihood of thrombosis) real-time risk prediction model of hospital-associated venous thromboembolism in children with congenital heart disease
evidence.outcome: Discrimination of the general pediatric model when applied to CHD subpopulation
evidence.effect: AUROC fell from 0.908 (all pediatric patients) to 0.801 in the CHD cohort; refitting improved it to 0.846.
evidence.quote: Overall, there was a slight decrease in discrimination compared to the CLOT model’s performance for all pediatric patients (AUROC = 0.908[0.896–0.918]; Figure 2 ).

evidence.title: The Vienna Prediction Model for identifying patients at low risk of recurrent venous thromboembolism: a prospective cohort study
evidence.outcome: Calibration of the VPM in a new prospective cohort
evidence.effect: Calibration adequate at 1 year, but the model underestimated 2-year risk above 5%; O/E ratio 52/32 = 1.6 (95% CI 1.2–2.0); calibration slope 1.3 (95% CI 0.3–2.4).
evidence.quote: The ratio of observed and expected events (O/E ratio), equal to 52/32 = 1.6 (95% CI 1.2–2.0), indicated general underestimation of recurrence probabilities.

evidence.title: The incremental design of a machine learning framework for medical records processing
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
evidence.outcome: Model performance over time as new clinics were onboarded
evidence.effect: Expanding to new clinics correlated with performance decline
evidence.quote: Expanding to new clinics correlated with performance decline, which was mitigated through model retraining.

evidence.title: Behind the Curtain: Comparing Predictive Models Performance in 2 Publicly Insured Populations
evidence.outcome: Performance when model transferred to a new population without re-evaluation
evidence.effect: Risk factors and weightings differed, sometimes dramatically, across populations; unadapted model applied to Medicaid performed poorly.
evidence.quote: However, the most salient risk factors and their relative weightings differed, sometimes dramatically, across the 2 populations.

evidence.title: Prospective Validation of a Suicide Event Risk Model in Transgender Patients
evidence.venue: AMIA ... Annual Symposium proceedings. AMIA Symposium
evidence.outcome: General-population model performance when applied to transgender patients
evidence.effect: The general population-trained model showed limited clinical utility in transgender patients: false negatives 77%, AUROC=0.777, AUPRC=0.115, and significant miscalibration (Brier=0.023, Spiegelhalter's z-statistic p<0.001).
evidence.quote: Findings underscore the importance of targeted subgroup validation and highlight limitations of general population-trained models in accurately identifying suicide risk among transgender patients.

evidence.title: AI-ECG Detection of Structural Heart Disease in the Community Setting: Transportability and Spectrum Effects in the PREVUE-VALVE Study
evidence.venue: Journal of the American College of Cardiology
evidence.outcome: Model performance when extended to a new population with lower prevalence and milder disease
evidence.effect: AUC 71% in community-dwelling adults vs 83% in hospital cohort; higher in subgroups with abnormal ECG (79%) or impaired health status (76%).
evidence.quote: In a community-dwelling population with lower disease prevalence and milder phenotypes, AI-ECG performance was attenuated relative to hospital-based cohorts, driven by differences in disease spectrum.
evidence.sample_unit: community-dwelling participants aged 65-85 with in-home ECG and echocardiography

evidence.title: Ranking-optimized survival models can underperform fixed-horizon clinical prediction
evidence.outcome: Generalization to disease groups absent from training (leave-one-disease-out validation)
evidence.effect: Severe generalization failure in disease groups absent from training.
evidence.quote: Leave-one-disease-out validation revealed severe generalization failure in disease groups absent from training.

evidence.title: External Validation and Calibration Assessment of Explainable Machine Learning Models for GVHD Prediction After Allogeneic HSCT
evidence.outcome: Model performance generalization to new external populations
evidence.effect: External AUROC fell to 0.51–0.57 for acute GVHD and 0.54–0.64 for chronic GVHD, with calibration overestimation in 10 of 11 combinations.
evidence.quote: Per-cohort recalibration is required before clinical deployment, with prospective validation and benchmarking against established GVHD risk scores identified as priority next steps.
evidence.country: United States, UAE, Jordan (multi-country registry cohorts)

evidence.title: Haemodynamic intolerance at the de-resuscitation decision in critically ill adults: development, temporal and external validation of a prediction model across two intensive care databases
evidence.outcome: Performance generalization to new populations
evidence.effect: Portable discrimination but prevalence-dependent calibration across time and populations.
evidence.quote: A model predicting haemodynamic intolerance at the de-resuscitation decision showed portable discrimination but prevalence-dependent calibration that was largely correctable by simple recalibration.

evidence.title: Machine learning for elective caesarean section in Bangladesh: validation design, not model choice, determines the performance a deployed model would have
evidence.outcome: Performance loss when model fitted to 2019 applied to 2025 round
evidence.effect: A model fitted to 2019 data lost 0.083 AUC when applied to 2025; predictor importance agreement was moderate (Spearman 0.61).
evidence.quote: A model fitted to 2019 data lost 0.083 when applied to 2025, and the two rounds agreed only moderately on which predictors mattered (Spearman rank correlation 0.61).

evidence.title: Temporal External Validation of Successive RCRI (Revised Cardiac Risk Index) Updates across Observational Healthcare Databases: a Multinational Retrospective Cohort Study
evidence.outcome: Generalization of RCRI to new databases and populations
evidence.effect: External validation on nine databases gave AUROC range 0.62–0.86 with calibration plots indicating overestimation of risk.
evidence.quote: In addition, we performed external validation on nine (including the eight used for temporal external validation) databases with an AUROC range of 0.62–0.86 and calibration plots that indicate an overestimation of risk.

evidence.title: Geographical validation of the Smart Triage Model by age group
evidence.outcome: Model performance in neonatal subgroup beyond original target population
evidence.effect: Neonates had poor discrimination (AUROC 0.62, 95% CI 0.55-0.70) and low-risk threshold sensitivity of 0.68 versus 0.85 for under-5
evidence.quote: However, a revised model is recommended for neonates due to their uniqueness in disease susceptibly, host response, and underlying physiological reserve.

evidence.title: Multisite evaluation of prediction models for emergency department crowding before and during the COVID-19 pandemic
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
evidence.outcome: extension to another hospital
evidence.effect: Transferred location2→1 model performed worse: AUC 0.51 vs 0.78 in COVID-era.
evidence.quote: Overall, our findings reinforce prior research that suggests models trained (or conceived) at one location and tested at another location may not perform well, and extreme care is needed when attempting to apply models across locations.
evidence.sample_unit: ED encounters (62,585 + 34,244 at location 1; 24,992 + 17,359 at location 2)

evidence.title: External validation and update of the J-ACCESS model in an Italian cohort of patients undergoing stress myocardial perfusion imaging
evidence.venue: Journal of nuclear cardiology : official publication of the American Society of Nuclear Cardiology
evidence.outcome: Model performance when applied to a new population (Italian vs Japanese cohort)
evidence.effect: J-ACCESS underestimated risk in Italian cohort; C-statistic 0.664 (0.632, 0.696); limited value for predicting three-year MACE.
evidence.quote: In general, the J-ACCESS model underestimates the observed data.

evidence.title: A recalibrated prediction model can identify level-1 trauma patients at risk of nosocomial pneumonia
evidence.venue: Archives of orthopaedic and trauma surgery
evidence.outcome: Generalization of predictive model to a new population and outcome definition
evidence.effect: Model developed for VAP in a US center underpredicted nosocomial pneumonia in a Dutch cohort; calibration slope 0.63.
evidence.quote: The calibration slope was 0.63, suggesting some overfitting in the original study compared to our population.

evidence.title: Validation in Indonesia of two published scores for mortality prediction after cardiac surgery
evidence.outcome: Generalization of predictive model to a new population
evidence.effect: EuroSCORE II and ACEF underestimated mortality in all risk groups and were poorly calibrated (HL P<0.001) in the Indonesian population
evidence.quote: The EuroSCORE II and ACEF score underestimated mortality in all risk groups, and both scores were poorly calibrated.

evidence.title: Decision-making support systems on extended hospital length of stay: Validation and recalibration of a model for patients with AMI
evidence.outcome: Model performance when applied to a new population/context
evidence.effect: Prior model applied to a new population lost predictive capacity (AUC 0.828 to 0.702; recall 72% to 58%), requiring recalibration.
evidence.quote: As a result, the model required recalibration in the population under study.

evidence.title: External validation of a deep learning detection system for glaucomatous optic neuropathy: a real-world multicentre study
evidence.outcome: Performance in a new population (high myopia) beyond the original use context
evidence.effect: In the high myopia subset, accuracy was 81.98% and AUC 87.49% (sensitivity 83.61%, specificity 81.76%), lower than the 93.18% accuracy and 95.17% AUC in dataset 1.
evidence.quote: In validation dataset 3, the algorithm achieved comparable accuracy of 81.98% and AUC of 87.49%, with a sensitivity of 83.61% and specificity of 81.76% on GON recognition specifically in the HM population.

evidence.title: Drug-related readmissions in older hospitalized adults: External validation and updating of OPERAM DRA prediction tool
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Geriatrics Society
evidence.outcome: original model discrimination, calibration, and overall accuracy
evidence.effect: scaled Brier score 0.03, C-statistic 0.62 (95% CI 0.59-0.64), and calibration showed underestimation of risks
evidence.quote: In the validation cohort, the original model showed a good overall accuracy (scaled Brier score 0.03), but discrimination was moderate (C-statistic 0.62 [95% CI 0.59-0.64]), and calibration showed underestimation of risks.

evidence.title: External validation of a lung cancer-based prediction model for two-year mortality in esophageal cancer patient cohorts
evidence.venue: Radiotherapy and oncology : journal of the European Society for Therapeutic Radiology and Oncology
evidence.outcome: Calibration and discrimination of lung cancer model when applied to esophageal cancer patients
evidence.effect: dCRT needed intercept adjustment (c-statistic 0.67, 95%CI 0.58 to 0.75); nCRT initial miscalibration (CS 1.72) required intercept and slope recalibration (c-statistic 0.62, 95%CI 0.57 to 0.67).
evidence.quote: For nCRT patients the model needed adjustment of both the slope and the intercept because of initial miscalibration in the validation population (CITL 0.00; CS 1.72).

evidence.title: External evaluation of the Dynamic Criticality Index: A machine learning model to predict future need for ICU care in hospitalized pediatric patients
evidence.outcome: Generalization of multi-institutional model to a new site not in development data
evidence.effect: Despite excellent performance in the multi-institutional dataset, AUROC fell to 0.493-0.545 and sensitivity to 0.007-0.008 at the new site.
evidence.quote: Despite excellent performance in an independent multi-institutional dataset [ 10 ], the multi-institutional models had substantially reduced performance in the single-site dataset.

evidence.title: Performance of a Machine Learning Algorithm to Predict Hypotension in Spontaneously Breathing Non-Ventilated Post-Anesthesia and ICU Patients
evidence.outcome: HPI hypotension prediction performance in non-ventilated PACU/ICU patients, a new population beyond ventilated patients
evidence.effect: AUC 0.94 overall; at threshold 85, sensitivity 1.00, specificity 0.79, PPV 0.85, NPV 1.00, median time-to-event 160 s. Performance not negatively affected in the non-ventilated population.
evidence.quote: The absence of positive pressure ventilation and the influence thereof on patient hemodynamics does not negatively affect the performance of the HPI algorithm in predicting hypotension in the PACU and ICU.

evidence.title: Development and external validation of the eFalls tool: a multivariable prediction model for the risk of ED attendance or hospitalisation with a fall or fracture in older adults
evidence.outcome: Calibration of model applied to new population (external validation)
evidence.effect: Model over-predicted risk in Bradford: pooled CITL -0.874 (95% CI -0.964 to -0.783), O/E 0.43 (95% CI 0.39 to 0.48); no better than treat-none at 10-25% thresholds.
evidence.quote: Calibration curves ( Figure 1 ) show that the eFalls model over-predicted fall/fracture risk in the Connect Bradford population, with predicted risks exceeding observed risks across the full range of possible predicted values.

evidence.title: Preparing for the bedside-optimizing a postpartum depression risk prediction model for clinical implementation in a health system
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
evidence.outcome: Model performance and fairness in a later year (COVID-19) and a different clinical research network population
evidence.effect: AUC remained high (0.94-0.97) across datasets, but fairness varied: biased on statistical parity in AMC data, generally unbiased in the clinical research network data.
evidence.quote: The findings revealed that the model exhibited biased performance in the AMC data but showed less bias in the clinical research network data, thus showing fairness metrics may vary across datasets.

evidence.title: Validation of a Multivariable Model to Predict Suicide Attempt in a Mental Health Intake Sample
evidence.outcome: Model performance when extended to a new use context (intake appointments)
evidence.effect: Model developed for any outpatient mental health visit showed good overall classification at intake (AUROC 0.77), but very low precision (AUPRC 0.02) given 0.17% base rate.
evidence.quote: In this prognostic study involving mental health intakes, a previously developed machine learning model of suicide attempts showed good overall classification performance.

evidence.title: Identifying potentially depressed older Chinese adults in the community: Hong Kong's Elderly Health Service cohort
evidence.outcome: Performance of European-developed model when applied to a new population (older Chinese adults)
evidence.effect: The original DRAT-up model underestimated risk of developing depressive symptoms in older Chinese adults; the new setting-specific model had better discrimination (C 0.68).
evidence.quote: The original DRAT-up model underestimated the risk of developing depressive symptoms in older Chinese adults; recalibrating it improved calibration.

evidence.title: Pitfalls of single-study external validation illustrated with a model predicting functional outcome after aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage
evidence.outcome: Generalizability to new cohorts
evidence.effect: Leeds membership model c-statistic 0.69, but discrimination was unsatisfactory, indicating poor generalizability.
evidence.quote: In the Leeds cluster the derivation and validation samples were similar (membership model c -statistic 0.69), but the discriminative performance was unsatisfactory indicating poor generalizability of the model (Supplementary Material 7).

evidence.title: Metabolic syndrome risk prediction in an Australian sample with first-episode psychosis using the psychosis metabolic risk calculator: A validation study
evidence.venue: Australasian psychiatry : bulletin of Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists
evidence.outcome: Model performance when applied to a new population (Australia)
evidence.effect: Original UK model under-predicted risk in Australian sample (calibration intercept 0.362 full model); C-statistics 0.72 and 0.71 vs UK 0.75 and 0.74.
evidence.quote: However, calibration plots demonstrated consistent under-prediction of risk.

evidence.title: Investigation of end-stage kidney disease risk prediction in an ethnically diverse cohort of people with type 2 diabetes: use of kidney failure risk equation
evidence.outcome: KFRE calibration when applied to a new endpoint (ESKD) and population (T2DM with CKD)
evidence.effect: KFRE under-predicted ESKD risk; underprediction worse for eGFR<15 endpoint than eGFR<10, despite good discrimination (C-index 0.843 at 2y, 0.801 at 5y).
evidence.quote: With the threshold 15 mL/min defining the study event, we also observed an underprediction of the 2-year and 5-year risks, but it was more significant compared with what was found with the primary event definition ( table 2 and online supplemental figure S3 ).

evidence.title: Performance of Machine Learning Suicide Risk Models in an American Indian Population
evidence.outcome: Model performance when extended to new population (majority American Indian)
evidence.effect: MHRN AUROC 0.81 for 90-day attempts and 0.86 for death, but VU only 0.68 and 0.63; all models poorly calibrated initially.
evidence.quote: The MHRN model was significantly more accurate than the VU model.

evidence.title: The value of local validation of a predictive model. A nomogram for predicting failure of non-invasive ventilation in patients with SARS-COV-2 pneumonia
evidence.outcome: Generalizability to other ICUs
evidence.effect: Validation AUC was 0.547 (CI 0.449-0.645); authors concluded it may not apply to other ICUs.
evidence.quote: A predictive model using age, obesity, SOFA score, HR, and HACOR at 24 h predicts NIV failure in our COVID-19 patients but may not apply to other ICUs.

evidence.title: Consecutive prediction of adverse maternal outcomes of preeclampsia, using the PIERS-ML and fullPIERS models: A multicountry prospective observational study
evidence.outcome: Model discrimination and net benefit when extended to consecutive daily prediction beyond 48 h
evidence.effect: fullPIERS AUC-PRC stayed low (0.2-0.4); PIERS-ML AUC-PRC peaked at 0.65 on day 0 then decreased notably; decision curve advantage diminished over time.
evidence.quote: We observed deteriorating performance of both models over time.
evidence.country: Multicountry (Americas, sub-Saharan Africa, South Asia, Europe, Oceania)

evidence.title: International external validation of the SORG machine learning algorithm for predicting sustained postoperative opioid prescription after anterior cervical discectomy and fusion using a Taiwanese cohort of 1,037 patients
evidence.venue: The spine journal : official journal of the North American Spine Society
evidence.outcome: Performance of SORG-MLA when applied to a new country population
evidence.effect: Discrimination was good (AUROC 0.78, AUPRC 0.35) and Brier 0.033 vs null 0.040, but risk was overestimated, indicating incomplete generalization.
evidence.quote: The model demonstrated good discriminative ability, with an AUROC of 0.78 and an AUPRC of 0.35.

evidence.title: External Validation of SCORE2-Diabetes Risk Prediction Model in Chinese Patients with Diabetes
evidence.outcome: generalization to Chinese patients
evidence.effect: Original SCORE2-Diabetes underestimated risk by 30% in men and 50% in women before recalibration.
evidence.quote: The original SCORE2-Diabetes underestimated risk by 30% in men and 50% in women, whereas the recalibrated SCORE2-Diabetes using high-risk region scaling factor had the best calibration, overestimating risk by only 4% in men and underestimating by 7% in women.

evidence.title: Predictive performance of cardiovascular disease risk prediction models in older adults: a validation and updating study
evidence.outcome: Generalization of models developed in middle-aged adults to older adults
evidence.effect: Models developed for middle-aged populations needed updating to improve prediction in older adults; further external validation in diverse older populations recommended before clinical implementation.
evidence.quote: Updating models, by adjusting model coefficients to better reflect the characteristics and risk factors of older adults, improves CVD risk prediction in a large cohort of relatively healthy Caucasian population aged 70+.

evidence.title: A population-based recalibration method for updating survival neural networks models for cardiovascular risk prediction in United Kingdom and China
evidence.outcome: Calibration of UK-trained models when applied to a Chinese population
evidence.effect: All SNN models had C-indices>0.720 in both UKB and CHERRY validation sets but underpredicted risk for CHERRY populations by 60%.
evidence.quote: All SNN models demonstrated robust discrimination in both UKB and CHERRY validation sets (C-indices>0.720), but underpredicted risk for CHERRY populations by 60%.

evidence.title: Clinical Characteristics of Gastrointestinal Malignancy and Validation of the IDIOM Model Among Patients With Iron Deficiency Anemia in Thailand
evidence.venue: JGH open : an open access journal of gastroenterology and hepatology
evidence.outcome: Generalization of a UK-developed predictive model to a new population
evidence.effect: IDIOM showed AuROC 62.9% in Thai patients with extreme risk underestimation (CITL 3.47, slope 0.27); very-low-risk group still had 18.1% GI malignancy prevalence.
evidence.quote: Moreover, the calibration of the model in our cohort showed an extreme underestimation of the risk.

evidence.title: Development and recalibration of a multivariable type 1 diabetes prediction model for type 1 diabetes across multiple screening studies
evidence.outcome: Model calibration when applied to new screening population beyond development context
evidence.effect: Model discriminated comparably (3-year AUC 0.712 TrialNet vs 0.756 TEDDY) but was poorly calibrated in TrialNet (Brier 0.40) until recalibrated.
evidence.quote: As expected, given differences in cohort selection criteria, we observed consistent underestimation of the risk of type 1 diabetes in TrialNet (Additional File 2—Figure S5).
evidence.country: USA, Sweden, Germany, Finland (TEDDY); USA, Canada, Australia (TrialNet)

evidence.title: Evaluating a predictive model of tyrosine kinase inhibitor therapy failure in a European-type cohort: a step towards population-specific tools
evidence.outcome: Generalization of a predictive model to a new population
evidence.effect: Model developed in a Chinese cohort did not discriminate risk groups effectively in the French cohort; HRs much lower than reported.
evidence.quote: In conclusion, our study demonstrates the limitations of directly transposing predictive models developed in ethnically or clinically distinct populations and also offers new insights that could advance personalized treatment strategies in CP-CML.

evidence.title: Evaluating the impact of data biases on algorithmic fairness and clinical utility of machine learning models for prolonged opioid use prediction
evidence.outcome: Model performance when applied to new population (VHA) beyond development setting
evidence.effect: AUROC fell from 0.74 to 0.70, subgroup disparities increased, and net-benefit threshold range shifted from [0.1-0.5] to [0.2-0.6].
evidence.quote: This shows the model’s performance sensitivity to outcome distribution shifts in real-world settings.

evidence.title: Bias or Best Fit? A Comparative Analysis of the SEER and NCDB Data Sets in Single-model Machine Learning for Predicting Osteosarcoma Survival Outcomes
evidence.outcome: Generalization of models to a new population/data context
evidence.effect: External validation AUC <0.70 (0.56-0.67) vs internal 0.90-0.93, indicating failure to generalize.
evidence.quote: Cross-database application of models leads to poor predictive performance and should be avoided without revalidation.

evidence.title: Domain validation of the CRASH prognostic model for predicting 14-day mortality among patients and traumatic brain injury and intracranial hemorrhage in a Thai emergency department
evidence.outcome: Generalization of CRASH model to new population (TBI with ICH in Thai ED)
evidence.effect: Discrimination retained (AuROC 0.92/0.93) but systematic overestimation of mortality (CITL -0.916 Basic, -1.257 CT).
evidence.quote: These results suggest that the models systematically predict higher risks of 14-day mortality than observed, particularly in higher-risk groups.

evidence.title: External validation and logistic recalibration of POSSUM and P-POSSUM for predicting postoperative morbidity and mortality after elective hepatic resection
evidence.outcome: Performance of established generic risk models applied to a new specialized surgical population
evidence.effect: POSSUM/P-POSSUM showed fair discrimination and slopes below 1 in hepatic resection, needing recalibration.
evidence.quote: OOB bootstrap calibration showed slopes below 1 for all endpoints (clinically relevant morbidity: α 0.16, β 0.837, Brier 0.172; major morbidity: α − 0.051, β 0.907, Brier 0.215; mortality: α − 0.34, β 0.843, Brier 0.068), supporting the need for local model updating.

evidence.title: Performance of an adult-trained AI tool for intracranial hemorrhage detection on head CT in children aged 6-17 years
evidence.outcome: Performance when extending an adult-trained model to a new pediatric population
evidence.effect: Sensitivity 94.2%, specificity 94.7%, NPV 99.4%, but PPV only 62.5%; false positives from streak artifact (21.6%) and misclassified anatomy (18.6%).
evidence.quote: AI correctly identified ICH in cases missed by radiologists, but false positives were common, most often due to streak artifact (21.6%) and misclassified anatomy (18.6%).

evidence.title: External validation of the PREVENT risk score: performance and clinical utility in an Iranian population
evidence.outcome: Generalization of US-developed model to a new Iranian population
evidence.effect: PREVENT underestimated risk in Iranian men, needing recalibration; sensitivity 62.4% in men at 5% threshold before recalibration.
evidence.quote: However, the original model underestimated risk in Iranian men, indicating the need for recalibration to improve alignment with the local risk profile.
evidence.sample_unit: adults in a community-based cohort (Tehran Lipid and Glucose Study)

evidence.title: An artificial intelligence prediction model for optimizing patient selection for cardiac imaging for the investigation of suspected coronary artery disease
evidence.outcome: Performance of model when applied to new regions and time periods
evidence.effect: Performance predictably decreased in new regions and periods (AUROC 0.714 geographic; 0.670-0.737 temporal) versus 0.807 locally.
evidence.quote: Our study showed that while model performance predictably decreases when applied to new regions (rural vs. urban, academic vs. community hospital) or time periods (pre-pandemic, COVID 19 pandemic, and post-pandemic), performance recovers following model updating.
evidence.sample_unit: elective outpatients undergoing invasive coronary angiography

evidence.title: Multicenter validation and updating of the ELDER-ICU model for severity assessment in elderly critical illness
evidence.outcome: Generalization to new populations
evidence.effect: US/Austria AUROC 0.804-0.864; South Korea 0.753; China 0.698.
evidence.quote: While maintaining robust performance in US and Austrian cohorts (AUROC 0.804-0.864), significant drops occurred in Asian sites (South Korea: 0.753; China: 0.698).
evidence.sample_unit: ICU patients aged 65+ across eight representative validation cohorts (Table 1)
evidence.country: United States, Austria, South Korea, China

evidence.title: Performance of Machine Learning Models for Sepsis and Stroke Detection Using EMS Data
evidence.outcome: Performance of ED-triage ML models when extended to prehospital EMS data
evidence.effect: Majority-of-predictions sepsis model: 68% sensitivity, 86% specificity, F1 0.33; stroke model: 71% sensitivity, 94% specificity, F1 0.34. Feasible but modest, with a sensitivity-specificity trade-off across prediction rules.
evidence.quote: The "majority of predictions" model for sepsis demonstrated 68% sensitivity and 86% specificity (+LR: 5, -LR: 0.4; accuracy: 85%, F1: 0.33).

evidence.title: Performance of a Screening Mammography AI Algorithm Repurposed for Symptomatic Mammography in a Tertiary Outpatient Clinic
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy (AUC) of a screening-trained AI applied to a new symptomatic population
evidence.effect: AUC 0.96 (95% CI 0.86-1.00) overall in 156 breasts with 15 malignancies; performance did not fail to generalize, though single-center and small.
evidence.quote: In the overall cohort (156 breasts, including 15 breasts with malignancies), the AI algorithm achieved an AUC of 0.96 (95% CI: 0.86-1.00).

evidence.title: Qualified prediction system for allograft failure in real world settings: extended validation study
evidence.outcome: iBox performance when extended to new clinical contexts and longer prediction horizon
evidence.effect: C index 0.81 with race-free eGFR equations; 0.74-0.87 across recurrence, BK virus, and immunosuppressive strategies; 0.79 at 10 years.
evidence.quote: The model performed well with different race-free eGFR equations (C index 0.81), in various clinical scenarios, including disease recurrence and BK virus nephropathy, with different immunosuppressive strategies, such as calcineurin inhibitors and mTOR (mechanistic target of rapamycin) inhibitors (C index range 0.74-0.87), and when extending the prediction period to 10 years after risk evaluation (C index 0.79).
evidence.country: France, other European countries, United States/Canada, South America (multinational)

evidence.title: External Validation, Recalibration, and Extension of a Prediction Model of Early Acute Kidney Injury in Critically Ill Children Using Multicenter Data
evidence.outcome: Model performance generalization to new populations and sites
evidence.effect: Single-center model performance decreased on multicenter data; PDC model applied to PEDSNET-VPS had lower sensitivity and PPV at both cutpoints (AUROC 0.62, AUPRC 0.03).
evidence.quote: Sanchez-Pinto and Khemani ( 5 ) created a parsimonious score to predict early AKI from single-center data; when we applied this score across multicenter data, the performance decreased.

evidence.title: Predicting Treatment Response After Total Neoadjuvant Therapy for Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer
evidence.outcome: Calibration when model applied to a new target population and outcome (pcCR in W/W patients)
evidence.effect: Brier score worsened to 0.30 in the new W/W population and AUROC was 0.69; recalibration was needed to reach 0.17.
evidence.quote: At external validation in a cohort of 83 patients that are being managed with TNT+W/W (median age 57; 37% female), the model predicted pcCR with an AUROC 0.69 (95% CI 0.57-0.82), AUPRC 0.90 (95% CI 0.82-0.96), and Brier score of 0.30 (95% CI 0.26-0.33), improving to 0.17 with recalibration.

evidence.title: Development and external validation of a machine learning model for predicting post-CABG acute kidney injury: insights from MIMIC database and real-world cardiac surgery cohort
evidence.outcome: Generalization of ICU-trained model to a specialized cardiac surgery population
evidence.effect: General ICU model showed substantial cross-domain transferability gap; AUC 0.548 and PR-AUC 0.309 in cardiac surgery cohort.
evidence.quote: General-purpose ICU models may face a substantial cross-domain transferability gap without local adaptation when applied to specialized sub-specialties like cardiac surgery across different demographic populations.
evidence.sample_unit: patients (external validation cohort; 6,347 in MIMIC development cohort)

evidence.title: External validation of machine learning models for estimation of mortality 1, 3, 6, and 12 months after hip fracture on 5,055 consecutive patients
evidence.outcome: Generalization of a predictive model to a new independent cohort

commentary.bottom_line: Four offline studies found that re-evaluating a model in a new health system, region, or subpopulation revealed losses in discrimination or calibration, and three found that updating recovered part or all of the loss. No study measured whether re-evaluation before extension changed patient outcomes, so the evidence shows that the check detects problems, not that it prevents harm.

perspectives.view: All four tests were retrospective or benchmark analyses at levels 4 and 5, and all were run offline. They agree in direction. AUC fell to 0.60 in a new health system, and AUROC fell from 0.908 to 0.801 in a congenital heart disease cohort. Certainty is low because the designs were descriptive and no test reached patients.

Hazard studies report large failures. AUROC fell to 0.493 to 0.545, with sensitivity near 0.008, at a new pediatric site, and false negatives reached 77% in transgender patients. In the tests, re-evaluation caught miscalibration before use, which suggests it may intercept such errors. No test tracked harm averted.

In a Hong Kong primary care cohort, the original model underestimated risk (intercept 1.79, slope 0.74). Simple recalibration corrected this, and AUC stayed between 0.742 and 0.750. In a multistate obstetric study, modest updating yielded well-calibrated models with AUC 0.69 to 0.70. Neither study reported the staff time the work required.

One test of 880,799 deliveries included Medicaid, rural, and racial and ethnic minority populations. It found that a New York City model overestimated risk in South Carolina and Florida until it was updated. A hazard study found that an unadapted model performed poorly when applied to Medicaid. No test included limited English proficiency or low-literacy patients.

Hazard studies linked performance decline to onboarding new clinics and to moving models between hospitals. The tested remedies used retrospective local data and simple recalibration, which suggests modest analytic effort. No study reported the cost, staffing, or time needed to repeat evaluation for each new site or population.

commentary.research_gap: No study tested re-evaluation before extension in a live deployment, and none compared patient outcomes, missed diagnoses, or clinician trust with and without the check. Prospective comparisons, cost and staffing data, and tests in limited English proficiency, low-literacy, and safety-net populations are absent.
commentary.underserved_note: One test, a multistate obstetric study of 880,799 deliveries, included Medicaid, rural, and racial and ethnic minority populations. No test included safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. Health systems that extend models to these groups therefore have no direct evidence on how much performance shifts or whether recalibration restores it.
